title: Heart palpitations
claims: Heart palpitations are common and not usually a sign of anything serious; they can be triggered by strenuous exercise, lack of sleep, stress, medicines, alcohol, caffeine, nicotine or recreational drugs.
Some people get palpitations during the menopause.
The NHS advises seeing a GP if palpitations keep coming back or get worse, last longer than a few minutes, or occur with a heart condition or a family history of heart problems.
The NHS advises calling 999 or going to A&E if palpitations occur with chest pain, shortness of breath, or feeling faint or fainting.
